subject.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels

question: What model-visible trust contract should CLI reseed history use for persisted group sender identity: an explicitly untrusted display label, a stable sender identifier with owner status, or the current plain `User (name)` form?
rationale: The renderer changes a model-visible identity boundary, and source inspection cannot determine whether maintainers intend mutable channel names to be treated as descriptive metadata or authoritative participant identity.

options.title: Preserve Explicit Trust Semantics
options.body: Use only contracted persisted fields and render the attribution as untrusted metadata, incorporating `senderIsOwner` only if the transcript contract explicitly approves it.

options.title: Approve Display-Only Labels
options.body: Keep `User (name)` but formally document and test that the label is descriptive only and never participates in authorization or owner inference.

options.title: Defer Historical Attribution
options.body: Pause this renderer change until one shared historical sender-attribution contract defines stable identity, display text, and owner semantics across consumers.

recommendation.title: Preserve Explicit Trust Semantics
recommendation.body: Use only contracted persisted fields and render the attribution as untrusted metadata, incorporating `senderIsOwner` only if the transcript contract explicitly approves it.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the durable sender envelope and its security/redaction contract, making them the strongest technical routing candidate for this identity-source decision.
